raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

**My reasoning (as the farmer):**

I'm 57 now, been working these 14 mu for twenty years. I split the land — about 8 mu in cotton on the sandier piece west of the house, and the other 6 mu I do wheat then maize, same as my wife's brother next door. Cotton's the main thing here in our village, that's how it's always been.

We got 8 mouths in the house but two of the younger ones are working in Handan and send a little back. My wife and I do most of the field work. Money is still tight — I can't go buying fancy inputs.

**Cotton (8 mu):** I'll plant around April 25th when the soil warms up proper. The seed shop has that improved variety everybody uses, about 30 yuan a mu. Before planting I put down one bag — 40 kg — of compound 15-15-15 per mu. Then at flowering I topdress maybe 15 kg urea. That's how I've always done it. Two well irrigations: one to wet the seedbed, one at flowering. I spray when I see aphids or bollworm, can't skip that.

**Wheat (6 mu):** Already in the ground since last October. Used about 35 kg of compound at sowing. Now I need to topdress around 12 kg urea per mu at jointing, and irrigate twice more — once for green-up now, once at heading. Harvest early June.

**Maize (6 mu, after wheat):** Very tight — maybe 3-4 days between wheat harvest and planting. I rent the small planter from the village cooperative, 30 yuan a mu. About 30 kg compound at planting, 10 kg urea at large-flare stage. One irrigation if July is dry. Harvest end of September.

I'm not changing much from last year. My neighbor cut his fertilizer last year and said yield dropped, so I'll stick with what works. Weather looks normal so far.
